stem: A discrete random variable X has the probability distribution: P(X=0)=0.20, P(X=1)=0.30, P(X=2)=0.35, P(X=3)=0.15. What is P(X >= 2)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.35 is only P(X=2); the student ignores P(X=3) and reports only one of the two terms.
0.65 = 1 - 0.35 applies the complement incorrectly to just P(X=2), not to the full complement P(X < 2) = 0.50.
0.15 is only P(X=3); the student ignores P(X=2) and reports only the second term.

explanation: P(X >= 2) sums the probabilities of all outcomes where X equals 2 or more. Only X=2 and X=3 qualify: 0.35 + 0.15 = 0.50.

explanation_sections.punchline: P(X >= 2) = P(X=2) + P(X=3) - include every outcome in the event, not just one.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: discrete PMF, tail probability query. Decisive move: identify all values in the event {X >= 2} = {2, 3} and sum their probabilities directly. Alternatively use complement: 1 - P(X=0) - P(X=1) = 1 - 0.20 - 0.30 = 0.50.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(X >= k) includes all values from k upward; sum them all or use the complement of P(X < k).
explanation_sections.timing: 45 seconds. Trap: reporting 0.35 alone (only P(X=2)). Both X=2 and X=3 must be included.
